en.headline: Police find no tampering in sports drinks after students fell ill
en.dek: Tests showed no foreign or toxic substances in the free bottles handed out near a Kwun Tong school athletics meet; the reported pinholes were design features of the packaging.
body: Hong Kong police said on Wednesday they found no evidence that anyone had deliberately tampered with bottled sports drinks linked to the illness of 16 secondary-school students.

The teenagers from Maryknoll Secondary School in Kwun Tong reported dizziness, vomiting and diarrhoea after drinking free bottles of the drink during lunch at an athletics meet at Hammer Hill Road Sports Ground on Tuesday. All have since been discharged from hospital with no signs of poisoning.

Senior Superintendent Hung Ngai of the East Kowloon crime formation said laboratory tests of the contents revealed no abnormal substances and no unknown liquids had entered the bottles. Officers also found no evidence that the plastic bottles had been deliberately pierced.

The force explained that the packaging uses a tear-off label design with two dotted lines of tiny perforations to aid recycling. The bottles had been chilled in an ice bath before distribution; when squeezed, residual water trapped between the bottle and label could force out through the holes, creating the appearance of leaks or pinholes.
Police said they would continue to examine other possible causes of the students’ symptoms, including exertion from the sports day, food consumed that day and the hygiene of the ice containers used.

zh.headline: 學生飲免費運動飲品不適 警方指無發現遭人破壞
zh.dek: 東九龍總區刑事總部表示，化驗結果無異常物質，包裝上的「針孔」實為易撕線設計，冰水積聚後按壓會滲出。
body: 警方周三表示，經調查後無證據顯示有人刻意破壞派發給學生的運動飲品膠樽，亦無發現不明液體注入樽內。
觀塘瑪利諾中學16名學生周二在斧山道運動場舉行運動會期間，飲用場外免費派發的運動飲品後出現頭暈、嘔吐及腹瀉等不適，全部已出院，並無中毒跡象。
東九龍總區刑事總部高級警司洪毅指，將檢獲飲品送交政府化驗所進行物理及毒理化驗，結果無異常。包裝設有易撕線，由細小孔連成，飲品派發前浸泡冰水，冰水積聚在樽身與標籤之間，用力按壓時積水會由易撕線滲出甚至射出，造成疑似針孔或滲漏的觀感。
警方表示，學生不適可能與激烈運動、當日進食食物或盛載冰塊膠桶的衞生情況有關，會繼續跟進。
